assessment.intent: A practical, locally grounded guide for service businesses that want more website enquiries to become booked work. It focuses on the operational handoff after the form is submitted: ownership, response capacity, qualification and simple automation.
assessment.specificity: High for the target reader. It names concrete pipeline stages, gives a mock six-step workflow, distinguishes manual, systematized and automated follow-up, and connects the advice to Michael's web design and AI implementation services without inventing client results.
assessment.evidence: Moderate. It cites W3C accessibility guidance for short, simple forms and otherwise relies on reasoned operational advice rather than statistics. The article avoids fabricated percentages, client anecdotes and guaranteed outcomes; its example workflow is explicitly labelled as mock.
assessment.voice: Conversational, direct and personally opinionated in Michael's style. It uses Canadian spelling, short connected sentences, and first-person references to his design and AI work. There is no corporate padding and no smug contrast.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. A service business owner could use it as a practical checklist for auditing their enquiry-to-booking handoff. The advice is constructive, mostly free of overclaiming, and points naturally to a consultation without overselling.
